Semantics is generally the content of what is being said or written, while syntax is the way in which it is said or written. The most obvious example I can quickly think of is programming. The semantics would be describing what a line of code is doing, while the syntax would be the way in which it must be written for it to work correctly.

edit: Just to extend the analogy to make it more clear what I meant...

x = y;

Semantics: the value of y is being stored in x

Syntax: the target operand must be before the equals sign (or assignment) and the operand from which the value is being retrieved must be after the equals sign. It must all be followed by a semi-colon
